description: Single-panel line plot (no micrographs present) showing Schmid factor evolution with tensile deformation at RT and LNT. Y-axis is labelled "Schmid factor" with ticks 0.41, 0.42, 0.43, 0.44, 0.45; x-axis is labelled "Engineering strain" with ticks 0.0-0.6 in 0.1 steps (i.e. 0-60 %). Four series are defined in the legend: RT {111}<110>_γ (black squares), RT {111}<112>_γ (red circles), LNT {111}<110>_γ (blue up-triangles) and LNT {111}<112>_γ (green down-triangles); markers sit near strains of ~0.00, ~0.03, ~0.10, ~0.28, ~0.44 and ~0.55, matching the caption's RT (3, 28, 44 %) and LNT (3, 10, 28, 55 %) levels. No numeric values are printed on the points, so all values are read against gridlines. The black RT {111}<110> curve rises marginally at ~3 % then drops steeply into the 0.42-0.43 band by ~10 % and continues down to the lowest RT value (near 0.414) at ~44 %. The red RT {111}<112> curve starts just below 0.445, falls to roughly 0.434 and stays nearly flat to ~28 % before declining to about 0.426, staying above black at every strain. Both LNT curves peak at ~10 % strain - green {111}<112> touches the 0.45 gridline and is the highest point of the figure, blue {111}<110> peaks just above 0.445 - then fall; blue ends lowest of all (near 0.41) at ~55 %, whereas green turns slightly upward. The figure therefore shows slip-favourable {111}<110> Schmid factors peaking early (3 % RT, 10 % LNT) with twinning-favourable {111}<112> Schmid factors dominating thereafter, especially at RT.

observations.observation: The image is a single line plot with y-axis 'Schmid factor' (ticks 0.41-0.45) and x-axis 'Engineering strain' (ticks 0.0-0.6 in 0.1 steps), i.e. strain plotted as a fraction from 0 to 60 %.
Four series are present, identified by the legend as RT {111}<110>_γ (black squares), RT {111}<112>_γ (red circles), LNT {111}<110>_γ (blue up-triangles) and LNT {111}<112>_γ (green down-triangles).
No numeric data labels are printed on any marker or axis point; values can only be read against the 0.41-0.45 gridlines, so individual Schmid factor values are not stated by the figure itself.

The blue LNT {111}<110>_γ curve reaches its maximum between the 0.44 and 0.45 gridlines at the ~0.10 strain point, then decreases monotonically to the lowest value of any curve (just above the 0.41 gridline) at ~0.55 strain.

The green LNT {111}<112>_γ curve rises to the highest value in the whole figure (essentially at the 0.45 gridline) at ~0.10 strain, then declines and shows a slight up-turn at the largest strain (~0.55).

The black RT {111}<110>_γ curve rises slightly to ~0.03 strain and then drops sharply into the 0.42-0.43 band by ~0.10 strain, remaining flat to ~0.28 and declining to its lowest value (~0.414) at ~0.44 strain.

The red RT {111}<112>_γ curve lies above the black RT {111}<110>_γ curve at every plotted strain, i.e. the {111}<112>_γ Schmid factor exceeds the {111}<110>_γ Schmid factor at RT over the whole strain range shown.
The caption block states that the IPF panels (Fig. 3) correspond to 0 %, 3 %, 28 % and 44 % engineering strains at RT and 3 %, 10 %, 28 % and 55 % engineering strains at LNT.

The supplied caption block also carries the caption of Fig. 3 (EBSD IPF maps of austenite along the TA direction after different tensile strains) although no IPF map or micrograph is present in the supplied image - the image contains only the Schmid factor plot.

The citing text assigns the black, red, blue and green lines to the evolution of the average {111}<110>_γ Schmid factor at RT, {111}<112>_γ Schmid factor at RT, {111}<110>_γ Schmid factor at LNT and {111}<112>_γ Schmid factor at LNT, respectively, matching the printed legend.

The citing text asserts that the average {111}<110>_γ Schmid factor at RT reaches its maximum near 3 % tensile strain while the average {111}<112>_γ Schmid factor at RT decreases at the same strain, which the plot supports as the black curve peaking at the lowest strain points while the red curve drops.

The citing text states that both the average {111}<110>_γ and {111}<112>_γ Schmid factors at LNT reach their maximum values at approximately 10 % engineering strain, matching the blue and green maxima seen at the ~0.10 x-tick.

The citing text attributes the RT crossing/dominance of the {111}<112>_γ Schmid factor over {111}<110>_γ to the development of <111>//TA and <100>//TA textures; this texture information is not shown in this figure.

subfigures.description: Line plot of Schmid factor (y, 0.41-0.45) versus engineering strain (x, 0.0-0.6) with four curves: RT {111}<110>_γ (black squares), RT {111}<112>_γ (red circles), LNT {111}<110>_γ (blue up-triangles), LNT {111}<112>_γ (green down-triangles). Both LNT curves peak near 0.10 strain; RT {111}<110> collapses after ~3 % strain; RT {111}<112> stays above RT {111}<110> throughout. No data labels are printed.
